elaine_marketing: Quick ask — marketing needs validated benchmark numbers for the launch blog + webinar. Can runtime run a focused sanity rerun for the three headline claims (gen latency p50/p95, embed p95, and cost-per-1k-tokens) across FP16 and the quantized profile? Need clear artifacts, raw traces, and acceptance criteria. Target: next Wed EOD if possible.

sam_runtime: We can do that. A couple quick clarifying q's: which exact model versions (names & hashes), which traffic profiles (slice definitions), and do you want cold-start measurements or steady-state only? Also do you need per-token breakdowns or just end-to-end latency? :eyes:

elaine_marketing: Thanks. Nominal scope we had in mind:
- Models: redwood-alpha-7b:fp16 (v2026-03-01) and redwood-alpha-7b:quant8 (v2026-03-05).
- Workloads: (A) chat gen — 8k microcohort of 1-turn prompts with target output ~150 tokens, (B) long-completion — 1k prompts ~1024-input / 512-output, (C) embeddings — 5k items, batch size 8.
- Sampling: stratified random sample across product cohorts (web, mobile, api) with 500 per slice for gen profiles where feasible.
- Metrics: p50/p90/p95 latency (server-side, token start->last token), cold-start p95 (first request after 5m idle), cost estimate per 1k tokens (using the usual model flops+HW cost assumptions), and CPU/GPU utilization heatmap.
- Artifacts: aggregated CSV, percentile curves, 50 raw request traces (annotated), and the run config + seed.

jess_marketing: We also need clear acceptance criteria for the marketing claims so legal/comms can sign off. Something like: p95 within X ms of our headline and cost within Y% of our stated number. Can runtime suggest sensible tolerances?

sam_runtime: For marketing-safe tolerances we usually recommend: p95 <= headline + 10% and cost delta <= 15% for quant vs fp16 when claiming parity. For cold-start callouts, we prefer explicit numbers rather than relative statements. We'll propose thresholds after a quick smoke.

michael_p: Where should runtime drop artifacts? We need an embargoed handoff so marketing can prep copy. Suggest s3 path with ACL: s3://redwood-internal/marketing/bench-1870000001/ and shared drive note. Also we need a simple short summary (1-paragraph) and the raw CSVs. Retention: keep artifacts for 30 days by default.

sam_runtime: Sounds good. We'll run a prioritised sanity flow: 1) smoke (50 samples each) for quick go/no-go, 2) full sweep (target sample counts above), 3) extract traces and cost calc. Estimated wall time: smoke ~2 hours, full sweep ~6-8 hours depending on queue. If you need faster, we can carve out burst nodes but that'll need approval.

elaine_marketing: Please proceed with the smoke today if possible. If smoke passes, full sweep next Tue night (low traffic window). If it fails, list what failed and whether we can adjust warmup or tweak model variant.

sam_runtime: On it. To make the runs reproducible, please confirm the canonical payload sets (we have the last marketing payload pack: s3://redwood-internal/marketing/payloads/launch-pack-v3.json). We will use seed=20260323 for deterministic RNG and include trace ids. Also confirm which metrics team should be cc'ed for regression alerts (we'll enable eval hooks).

elaine_marketing: Use launch-pack-v3.json. CC: @jess_marketing and @michael_p for artifacts. Also cc platform-metrics for regression alerts.

perf-bot: bench job queued — job id bench-1870000001-smoke. Estimated runtime 1h45m. You will be notified on completion.

sam_runtime: Quick note on measurement definitions so everything is explicit for legal/comms: 
- "server-side latency": time from request received by inference front-end to last byte of model output sent (excludes client parse/rt network).
- "cold-start": first in-VM request after >5 minute idle where runtime needs to warm KV cache / JIT kernels.
- "steady-state": after 30 warmup requests with continuous steady traffic.
- We'll provide both median & tail and a CSV with per-request fields: request_id, model, variant, seq_len_in, seq_len_out, tokens_generated, latency_ms, gpu_util, mem_used_mb, trace_link.

jess_marketing: Perfect. For the public blog we'll probably call out FP16 baseline and quantized improvements with a small note about test harness; legal prefers a single sentence about "internal benchmark methodology" linking to an appendix. Can you also include a one-line human-readable summary for each model (e.g., "redwood-alpha-7B quant8: ~12% cheaper at p95 with 5% p95 latency increase vs fp16")?

sam_runtime: Yes — we will draft the one-line summaries after the full sweep. For now smoke will output a draft sentence we can iterate on.

michael_p: One last operations ask — include the perf CLI command we used (so marketing can reproduce small checks):
```
redwood-bench run \
  --model redwood-alpha-7b:fp16 \
  --payload s3://redwood-internal/marketing/payloads/launch-pack-v3.json \
  --samples 50 \
  --seed 20260323 \
  --out s3://redwood-internal/marketing/bench-1870000001/smoke/
```

sam_runtime: Thanks — exact command for perf-bot: `perf-bot trigger bench-1870000001 --profile smoke --notify #marketing` (we'll post the exact job link when finished).

perf-bot: bench-1870000001-smoke completed — summary attached (s3://redwood-internal/marketing/bench-1870000001/smoke/summary.csv). Preliminary: fp16 p95 gen = 183ms, quant8 p95 gen = 200ms, embed p95 = 28ms. Raw traces uploaded.

elaine_marketing: Nice, thanks team. Can you add the preliminary one-liners for comms and we will iterate? Also add an embargo note and a recommended quote for the blog author.

sam_runtime: Draft one-liners (prelim):
- redwood-alpha-7B:fp16 — p95 gen 183ms (steady-state), cost baseline.
- redwood-alpha-7B:quant8 — p95 gen 200ms (+9% vs fp16), cost ~12% lower on this workload.
- embeddings — p95 28ms (batch8, steady-state).
We'll polish after full run. :thumbsup:

jess_marketing: This is great — will draft copy against these. If full sweep confirms, we'll lock the numbers and request a legal review.

michael_p: I've set the S3 ACL for the bench folder to embargo until 2026-04-02 and added platform-metrics to watchers. Leaving notes in the folder about retention.

elaine_marketing: Awesome — thank you all. Please ping if any blockers in the run.

sam_runtime: Will do. If anything surprising pops in the smoke we'll flag with root cause + mitigation suggestions.

perf-bot: tag:complete :white_check_mark:
